# Try to find gene names/symbols for missing values
```{r}
# --- Prerequisites ---
# Ensure you have the necessary packages installed.
# Run these lines in your R console if you haven't installed them before:

#     install.packages("BiocManager")

# Load the required libraries
library(biomaRt)
library(dplyr)
library(progress) # Optional, but helpful for long queries

# --- Load your counts data ---
# Assuming your data frame is already loaded and named 'counts'
# If loading from the featureCounts file:
# counts_file <- "/vast/projects/Immune_Aging/Itokawa_et_al_2022_RNAseq/featureCounts/gene_counts_HSCs_MPPs_etc_with_gene_names.txt"
# counts <- read.table(counts_file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", comment.char = "#", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# data_colnames <- grep("^SRR", colnames(counts), value = TRUE) # Get only data columns
# clean_colnames <- gsub("^_", "", gsub(".bam$", "", gsub(".*part2.", "", data_colnames))) # Example cleaning
# colnames(counts)[match(data_colnames, colnames(counts))] <- clean_colnames

# Check initial state
print("Original data dimensions:")
print(dim(counts))
print(paste("Initial number of NA gene names:", sum(is.na(counts$gene_name))))
print("Columns before enrichment:")
print(colnames(counts))

# --- Connect to Ensembl using biomaRt ---
print("Connecting to Ensembl BioMart...")
tryCatch({
  ensembl_mart <- useMart(biomart = "ENSEMBL_MART_ENSEMBL",
                          host = "https://www.ensembl.org")
  ensembl_mart <- useDataset(dataset = "mmusculus_gene_ensembl", mart = ensembl_mart)
  print("Connected successfully.")
}, error = function(e) {
  message("Error connecting to Ensembl. Check internet connection or Ensembl status.")
  message("Original error: ", e$message)
  stop("BioMart connection failed.")
})


# --- Prepare Ensembl IDs ---
# Get unique Ensembl IDs from your counts table
ensembl_ids <- unique(counts$Geneid)
# Optional: Remove potential version suffixes (e.g., ".1") if they exist
# ensembl_ids <- gsub("\\..*$", "", ensembl_ids)
print(paste("Number of unique Ensembl IDs to query:", length(ensembl_ids)))

# --- Query BioMart ---
# Define the attributes we want to retrieve
attributes_to_get <- c(
  "ensembl_gene_id",  # The ID we are using to query
  "entrezgene_id",    # Entrez Gene ID
  "mgi_symbol",       # The common gene symbol from MGI
  "mgi_id"            # The MGI database ID
)

# Define the filter (what we are searching by)
filters_to_use <- "ensembl_gene_id"

print("Querying BioMart for Entrez IDs, MGI symbols, and MGI IDs...")
# Estimate chunks if querying a very large number of IDs (e.g., > 5000)
# chunk_size <- 2000
# id_chunks <- split(ensembl_ids, ceiling(seq_along(ensembl_ids)/chunk_size))
# gene_info_list <- list()

# Initialize progress bar
# pb <- progress_bar$new(

# Perform the query (can take a few minutes for many genes)

#   pb$tick()
# }
# Combine results from chunks
# gene_info <- bind_rows(gene_info_list)

# Single query (usually fine for < ~20k IDs)
tryCatch({
 gene_info <- getBM(

   filters    = filters_to_use,
   values     = ensembl_ids,
   mart       = ensembl_mart
 )
}, error = function(e){
```

```{r}
# --- Process BioMart results ---
print("Processing BioMart results...")
# 1. Handle cases where MGI might be NA or empty strings ""
#    NOTE: Removed the line for entrezgene_id as it's integer and doesn't contain "".
gene_info <- gene_info %>%
  dplyr::mutate( # Explicitly use dplyr::mutate
    # entrezgene_id = na_if(entrezgene_id, ""), # Removed this line in previous step
    mgi_symbol = na_if(mgi_symbol, ""),
    mgi_id = na_if(mgi_id, "")
  ) %>%
  # Ensure EntrezID is character for flexibility later if needed, handle actual NAs
  dplyr::mutate(entrezgene_id = as.character(entrezgene_id)) # Explicitly use dplyr::mutate

# 2. Remove duplicated Ensembl IDs (e.g., if one Ensembl ID maps to multiple Entrez IDs)
#    Keep the first match found by BioMart. Prioritize rows with MGI symbols if deciding between duplicates.
gene_info <- gene_info %>%
  dplyr::arrange(ensembl_gene_id, desc(!is.na(mgi_symbol))) %>% # Explicitly use dplyr::arrange
  dplyr::filter(!duplicated(ensembl_gene_id))                   # Explicitly use dplyr::filter

print(paste("Retained info for", nrow(gene_info), "unique Ensembl IDs after processing."))
# head(gene_info) # Optional check

# --- Merge BioMart info with the counts table ---
print("Merging BioMart information with counts table...")
# Select only necessary columns before join to avoid duplicate info columns
# --- CORRECTED LINE using dplyr::select ---
counts_orig_info <- counts %>% dplyr::select(Geneid, Chr, Start, End, Strand, Length, gene_name, gene_biotype)

# Assuming count columns start with SRR or similar pattern, adjust if needed
# --- CORRECTED LINE using dplyr::select and tidyselect helpers ---
counts_data <- counts %>% dplyr::select(Geneid, matches("^SRR")) # Use tidyselect helper

# Check if the selection worked
if(nrow(counts_orig_info) == 0 || ncol(counts_orig_info) < 8) {
    stop("Selection of original info columns failed. Check column names in 'counts'.")
}
if(nrow(counts_data) == 0 || ncol(counts_data) < 2) {
    stop("Selection of count data columns failed. Check column names starting with 'SRR'.")
}


# Join annotation info fetched from biomart
counts_annotated <- dplyr::left_join(counts_orig_info, gene_info, by = c("Geneid" = "ensembl_gene_id"))

# Join back the count data
counts_final <- dplyr::left_join(counts_annotated, counts_data, by = "Geneid")

# Check columns after merge
print("Columns after merging:")
print(colnames(counts_final))
# head(counts_final) # Optional: view merged data

# --- Fill missing original gene_name values ---
# (This part remains the same as it uses base R indexing)
# Step 1: Fill NA 'gene_name' with 'mgi_symbol' where available
print("Attempting to fill missing original gene names using fetched MGI symbols...")
initial_na_count <- sum(is.na(counts_final$gene_name))
# Need to check if mgi_symbol column exists after join
if("mgi_symbol" %in% colnames(counts_final)) {
    indices_to_fill_mgi <- which(is.na(counts_final$gene_name) & !is.na(counts_final$mgi_symbol))
    if(length(indices_to_fill_mgi) > 0) {
      counts_final$gene_name[indices_to_fill_mgi] <- counts_final$mgi_symbol[indices_to_fill_mgi]
      print(paste("Filled", length(indices_to_fill_mgi), "gene names using MGI symbols."))
    } else {
      print("No missing gene names could be filled using available MGI symbols.")
    }
} else {
     print("Column 'mgi_symbol' not found after merge. Skipping fill step.")
}
print(paste("NA gene names remaining after MGI fill:", sum(is.na(counts_final$gene_name))))

# Step 2: Fill remaining NA 'gene_name' with the 'Geneid' (Ensembl ID)
print("Filling any remaining missing gene names with Ensembl Gene IDs as fallback...")
indices_to_fill_ensembl <- which(is.na(counts_final$gene_name))

if(length(indices_to_fill_ensembl) > 0) {
  counts_final$gene_name[indices_to_fill_ensembl] <- counts_final$Geneid[indices_to_fill_ensembl]
  print(paste("Filled", length(indices_to_fill_ensembl), "gene names using Ensembl IDs."))
} else {
  print("No remaining NA gene names to fill with Ensembl IDs.")
}

# Final check for NAs in gene_name
final_na_count <- sum(is.na(counts_final$gene_name))
print(paste("Final count of NA gene names:", final_na_count))
if(final_na_count > 0) {
    print("Warning: Some gene names are still NA after all steps. This should not happen with the fallback.")
}

# --- Finalize Columns ---
print("Finalizing columns...")
# Ensure column names from BioMart are handled correctly after the join
# --- CORRECTED LINE using dplyr::rename and dplyr::select ---
counts_final <- counts_final %>%
  dplyr::rename(EntrezID = entrezgene_id, MGI_ID = mgi_id) %>%
  # Reorder and remove temporary mgi_symbol. Adjust if columns differ.
  dplyr::select(Geneid, gene_name, gene_biotype, EntrezID, MGI_ID, Chr, Start, End, Strand, Length, matches("^SRR"), -any_of("mgi_symbol"))


print("Final columns reordered:")
print(colnames(counts_final))
print("Final data dimensions:")
print(dim(counts_final))
print("Sample of final data:")
print(head(counts_final))
```

```{r}
# Load the edgeR library
library(edgeR)
library(stringr) # For easier string manipulation if needed
library(dplyr)   # For easier data frame manipulation if needed

# Assuming your raw counts matrix is 'counts_data'
# Assuming your gene annotation data frame is 'counts_final'

# --- 1. Prepare Sample Information ---

# Extract sample information from column names
sample_names <- colnames(counts_data)

# Create a data frame to hold sample metadata
sample_info <- data.frame(
  SampleName = sample_names,
  # Extract Age (Young/Old) - Assumes format like "..._Age_..."
  Age = str_extract(sample_names, "(Young|Old)"),
  # Extract Cell Type - Assumes format like "..._CellType_..."
  CellType = str_extract(sample_names, "(HSC|MPP1|MPP2|MPP3|MPP4|GMP|MEP|CLP)"),
  # Extract Replicate - Assumes format like "..._RepX"
  Replicate = str_extract(sample_names, "Rep[0-9]+"),
  row.names = sample_names # Optional: set row names for easier matching
)

# Create a combined 'Group' factor for easier modeling initially
# This represents each unique combination of Age and CellType
sample_info$Group <- factor(paste(sample_info$Age, sample_info$CellType, sep = "_"))

sample_info
```

```{r}
# --- 2. Create DGEList Object and Add Gene Annotation ---

# Ensure gene IDs in counts_final match the rownames of counts_data
# It's CRUCIAL that the order of genes in counts_final matches the order
# of genes (rownames) in counts_data *after* creating the DGEList.

# Create the DGEList object
# We use the combined 'Group' factor here for initial setup
dge <- DGEList(counts = counts_data,
               group = sample_info$Group,
               samples = sample_info) # Add all sample info

# Add gene annotations from counts_final to dge$genes
# First, make sure the order matches
gene_order_match <- match(rownames(dge), counts_final$Geneid)

# Check if all gene IDs were found (optional but recommended)
if (any(is.na(gene_order_match))) {
  warning("Not all rownames in counts_data matched Geneid in counts_final!")
  # You might need to investigate missing/mismatched IDs here
}

# Reorder counts_final to match the DGEList rownames and select desired columns
dge$genes <- counts_final[gene_order_match,
                          c("Geneid", "gene_name", "gene_biotype",
                            "EntrezID", "MGI_ID", "Length")]

# Sanity check: verify row names of counts match Geneid in dge$genes
# print(head(cbind(rownames(dge$counts), dge$genes$Geneid)))
stopifnot(all(rownames(dge) == dge$genes$Geneid))

# Ensure the 'Length' column is numeric for RPKM calculation
dge$genes$Length <- as.numeric(dge$genes$Length)
if(any(is.na(dge$genes$Length))) {
    warning("Some gene lengths were NA or could not be converted to numeric. RPKM might be NA for these genes.")
}
head(dge$genes)
```

```{r}
# --- 3. Calculate RPKM Values (Before Filtering/Normalization) ---

# RPKM uses the original library sizes and requires gene lengths
# Ensure gene lengths are present and numeric (done in the previous step)
# Note: rpkm() uses library sizes from dge$samples$lib.size, which DGEList() calculates automatically
# from column sums of the counts matrix.

# Calculate RPKM for all genes and samples present *before* filtering
rpkm_matrix <- rpkm(dge, gene.length = dge$genes$Length)
```

########################
# DE analysis with edgeR
```{r}
# --- 4. Filtering Lowly Expressed Genes ---

# Define the design matrix based on the groups you want to keep track of.
# Using the combined 'Group' is suitable here for filtering across all conditions.
# The ~0+ formulation creates a coefficient for each group level without an intercept.
design <- model.matrix(~0 + Group, data = dge$samples)
colnames(design) <- levels(dge$samples$Group) # Make column names cleaner

# Use filterByExpr - it considers library sizes and the design matrix
# to suggest genes to keep. Minimum group size is automatically detected.
keep <- filterByExpr(dge, design = design)
dge_filtered <- dge[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE] # keep.lib.sizes=FALSE recalculates lib sizes

n_genes_before <- nrow(dge)
n_genes_after <- nrow(dge_filtered)
print(paste("Filtering removed", n_genes_before - n_genes_after, "genes."))
print(paste("Remaining genes:", n_genes_after))
```


```{r}
# --- 5. TMM Normalization ---

# Calculate normalization factors using the Trimmed Mean of M-values (TMM) method
# This accounts for library size and compositional differences.
# It calculates factors which adjust the library sizes used in downstream modeling.
dge_norm <- calcNormFactors(dge_filtered)

head(dge_norm$samples)
```


```{r}
saveRDS(dge_norm, file = "/vast/projects/Immune_Aging/Itokawa_et_al_2022_RNAseq/DEG_analysis_STAR_aligned_counts_all_cell_types/Itokawa_et_al_2022_RNAseq_STAR_aligned_counts_dge_TMM_norm.rds")
```



```{r}
# Plot MDS to visualize sample relationships after normalization
plotMDS(dge_norm, labels = dge_norm$samples$Group, col = as.numeric(dge_norm$samples$Group))
title("MDS Plot after TMM Normalization")
```


```{r}
# --- 6. Differential Expression Analysis (Old HSC vs Young HSC) ---

# edgeR's recommended approach is the Quasi-Likelihood F-test pipeline.
# We use the design matrix created earlier (~0 + Group).

# Estimate dispersions (common, trended, and tagwise/gene-wise)
# estimateDisp uses the design matrix. robust=TRUE is recommended.
dge_disp <- estimateDisp(dge_norm, design = design, robust = TRUE)

# Optional: Visualize dispersion estimates
# plotBCV(dge_disp)
# title("Biological Coefficient of Variation (BCV) Plot")

# Fit the Quasi-Likelihood Negative Binomial GLM
# This fits the model for each gene and estimates QL dispersions.
fit_ql <- glmQLFit(dge_disp, design = design, robust = TRUE)
```


```{r}
# Plot QL dispersions
plotQLDisp(fit_ql)
title("Quasi-Likelihood (QL) Dispersion Plot")
```


```{r}
# Define the contrast for the comparison of interest: Old HSC vs Young HSC
# We use makeContrasts based on the column names of the design matrix.
# The column names should be 'Old_HSC', 'Young_HSC', etc.
contrast_hsc <- makeContrasts(Old_vs_Young_HSC = Old_HSC - Young_HSC, levels = design)
print("Contrast matrix for Old HSC vs Young HSC:")
print(contrast_hsc)
```


```{r}
# Perform the Quasi-Likelihood F-test for the defined contrast
qlf_hsc <- glmQLFTest(fit_ql, contrast = contrast_hsc)
```

```{r}
# --- 7. View Results ---

# Get the table of top differentially expressed genes (ranked by FDR)
top_hsc_tags <- topTags(qlf_hsc, n = 20) # Show top 20
print("Top differentially expressed genes (Old HSC vs Young HSC):")
print(top_hsc_tags)
```


```{r}

# Get results for ALL tested genes, sorted by p-value
all_hsc_results <- topTags(qlf_hsc, n = Inf)$table
```


```{r}
head(all_hsc_results, n=20)
```


```{r}

OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05 <- all_hsc_results[all_hsc_results$FDR<0.05, ]

```


```{r}
# Create an MA plot (Smear plot in edgeR terms)
plotMD(qlf_hsc, main = "MA Plot: Old HSC vs Young HSC", cex=0.5, bg.cex=0.5)

```

Create genomic ranges object of significant DEGs
```{r}
# Load required packages
library(edgeR)
library(rtracklayer)

# Import the GTF file
gtf_file <- "/vast/projects/Immune_Aging/Reference_genomes/mm39/ensembl_release-113/Mus_musculus.GRCm39.113.gtf"
gtf <- import(gtf_file)

# Extract gene-level annotations
genes_gtf <- gtf[gtf$type == "gene"]
```


```{r}
# Create a data frame with genomic ranges
gene_ranges <- data.frame(
  Geneid = mcols(genes_gtf)$gene_id,
  seqnames = as.character(seqnames(genes_gtf)),
  start = start(genes_gtf),
  end = end(genes_gtf),
  strand = as.character(strand(genes_gtf)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

head(gene_ranges)
```


```{r}
# Merge genomic ranges with significant DEGs
OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_ranges <- merge(
  OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05,
  gene_ranges,
  by = "Geneid",
  all.x = TRUE
)

head(OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_ranges)
```

```{r}
# Read the chromosome lengths from the .fai file
fai_file <- "/vast/projects/Immune_Aging/Reference_genomes/mm39/ensembl_release-113/Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa.fai"
```

```{r}

# Then, ensure that the chromosome names in 'seqlengths_vector' match those in 'degs_granges'
common_seqnames <- intersect(seqlevels(degs_granges), names(seqlengths_fai))

# Subset 'seqlengths_fai' to include only the relevant chromosomes
seqlengths_to_add <- seqlengths_fai[common_seqnames]

# Set the seqlengths in your GRanges object
seqlengths(degs_granges) <- seqlengths_to_add

# Create a Seqinfo object
seqinfo_degs <- Seqinfo(
  seqnames = names(seqlengths_to_add),
  seqlengths = seqlengths_to_add,
  genome = "GRCm39"  # Specify the genome assembly
)

# Assign the Seqinfo object to your GRanges object
seqinfo(degs_granges) <- seqinfo_degs
seqinfo(degs_granges)
head(degs_granges)

```

# Heatmaps
Counts Per Million (CPM):
CPM is a normalization method that adjusts raw read counts by:
Accounting for library size differences (total number of reads per sample).
Scaling counts to a "per million" reads basis for comparability across samples.

Log Transformation:
CPM values are often log-transformed to:
Reduce the skew caused by highly expressed genes.
Stabilize variance across genes with differing expression levels.

Color Scale:
Blue (low logCPM): Indicates low expression.
Red (high logCPM): Indicates high expression.
White (middle values): Represents medium expression levels.
```{r fig.width=5, fig.height=10}
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)

# Log-transform normalized counts for heatmap
logCPM <- cpm(dge, log = TRUE)

rownames(OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges)<-OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges$Geneid

# Select top 50 DE genes by FDR for heatmap
top_genes <- head(OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges[order(OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges$FDR), ], 50)

# Extract the gene names for the top DE genes
top_gene_names <- top_genes$gene_name

# Subset logCPM for the top genes
heatmap_data <- logCPM[top_genes, ]

column_order <- order(group)

# Generate heatmap with gene names as row labels
Heatmap(
  heatmap_data,
  name = "logCPM",
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),  # Adjust font size if needed
  row_labels = top_gene_names,       # Use gene names as labels
  column_split = group,              # Split columns by group
  column_order = column_order,
  show_row_names = TRUE,             # Display row names (gene names)
  show_column_names = TRUE,          # Display column names (samples)
  cluster_columns = FALSE,            # Cluster columns
  cluster_rows = TRUE,                # Cluster rows
  col = colorRamp2(c(min(heatmap_data), 0, max(heatmap_data)), c("white", "pink", "purple")), #set colour range
  column_names_rot = 45              # Rotate column names by 45 degrees
  #clustering_distance_rows = "pearson",  # Use Pearson correlation for distance
  #clustering_method_rows = "complete"   # Use complete linkage for clustering
)

# Define the directory
plot_dir <- "/vast/projects/Immune_Aging/Itokawa_et_al_2022_RNAseq/DEG_analysis_STAR_aligned_counts_all_cell_types/Itokawa_et_al_2022_DEG_Plots"


# Get the current date
current_date <- Sys.Date()

# Create the full file paths with date prefix
pdf_file <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(current_date, "_top50_DEG_logCPM_Heatmap.pdf"))

# Open a new Cairo device with specified dimensions
library(Cairo)
CairoPDF(file = pdf_file, width=5, height=10, pointsize = 12, bg = "transparent", onefile = TRUE, canvas = "white")

# Generate heatmap with gene names as row labels
Heatmap(
  heatmap_data,
  name = "logCPM",
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),  # Adjust font size if needed
  row_labels = top_gene_names,       # Use gene names as labels
  column_split = group,              # Split columns by group
  column_order = column_order,
  show_row_names = TRUE,             # Display row names (gene names)
  show_column_names = TRUE,          # Display column names (samples)
  cluster_columns = FALSE,            # Cluster columns
  cluster_rows = TRUE,                # Cluster rows
  col = colorRamp2(c(min(heatmap_data), 0, max(heatmap_data)), c("white", "pink", "purple")), #set colour range
  column_names_rot = 45              # Rotate column names by 45 degrees
  #clustering_distance_rows = "pearson",  # Use Pearson correlation for distance
  #clustering_method_rows = "complete"   # Use complete linkage for clustering
)
dev.off()
```


Script for Heatmap with logFC
```{r fig.width=5, fig.height=10}
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)

# Select top 50 DE genes by FDR
top_de_genes <- head(OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges[order(OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges$FDR), ], 50)

# Extract logFC for the top genes
logFC_matrix <- matrix(top_de_genes$logFC, ncol = 1)
rownames(logFC_matrix) <- top_de_genes$gene_name
colnames(logFC_matrix) <- "logFC"

# Define color scale (red for upregulated, blue for downregulated)
col_fun <- colorRamp2(c(min(logFC_matrix), 0, max(logFC_matrix)),
                      c("blue", "white", "red"))

# Generate heatmap
Heatmap(
  logFC_matrix,
  name = "logFC",
  col = col_fun,
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 8),  # Adjust font size for row labels
  column_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 10),  # Adjust font size for column label
  cluster_rows = TRUE,  # Cluster genes
  show_column_names = TRUE,  # Show logFC as column name
  heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "logFC", legend_direction = "horizontal")
)

```

Combine logCPM and logFC: You can overlay the expression heatmap (logCPM) with annotations for logFC using a separate annotation bar.
```{r fig.width=5, fig.height=10}
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)

# Log-transform normalized counts for heatmap
logCPM <- cpm(dge, log = TRUE)

# Select top 100 DE genes by FDR for heatmap
top_genes <- head(rownames(OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges[order(OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges$FDR), ]), 100)

# Extract the gene names for the top DE genes
top_gene_names <- OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges$gene_name[match(top_genes, OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges$gene_id)]

# Select top 100 DE genes by FDR
top_de_genes <- head(OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges[order(OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges$FDR), ], 100)

# Extract logFC for the top genes
logFC_matrix <- matrix(top_de_genes$logFC, ncol = 1)
rownames(logFC_matrix) <- top_de_genes$gene_name
colnames(logFC_matrix) <- "logFC"

# Subset logCPM for the top DE genes
heatmap_data <- logCPM[top_genes, ]
rownames(heatmap_data) <- top_gene_names

# Define color functions
logCPM_col_fun <- colorRamp2(c(min(heatmap_data), 0, max(heatmap_data)), c("white", "pink", "purple"))
logFC_col_fun <- colorRamp2(c(min(top_de_genes$logFC), 0, max(top_de_genes$logFC)), c("blue", "white", "red"))

# Define row annotation for logFC
logFC_annotation <- rowAnnotation(
  logFC = anno_simple(
    top_de_genes$logFC,
    col = logFC_col_fun,
    width = unit(1, "cm")
  )
)

# Create heatmap
heatmap <- Heatmap(
  heatmap_data,
  name = "logCPM",
  right_annotation = logFC_annotation,
  col = logCPM_col_fun,
  row_names_gp = gpar(fontsize = 6),
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_columns = FALSE,
  column_order = order(group),
  show_column_names = TRUE,
  heatmap_legend_param = list(title = "logCPM", legend_direction = "horizontal"),
  column_names_rot = 45,
  column_title = "Top 100 DE genes, FDR<0.05",
  column_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 14)
)

# Add a separate legend for logFC
logFC_legend <- Legend(
  title = "logFC",
  col_fun = logFC_col_fun,
  at = c(min(top_de_genes$logFC), 0, max(top_de_genes$logFC)),
  labels = c("Downregulated", "No Change", "Upregulated"),
  legend_height = unit(1, "in")
)

# Combine the heatmap and additional legend
draw(heatmap, annotation_legend_list = list(logFC_legend), merge_legend = TRUE)

# Define the directory
plot_dir <- "/vast/projects/Immune_Aging/Itokawa_et_al_2022_RNAseq/DEG_analysis_STAR_aligned_counts_all_cell_types/Itokawa_et_al_2022_DEG_Plots"


# Get the current date
current_date <- Sys.Date()

# Create the full file paths with date prefix
pdf_file <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(current_date, "_top100_DEG_logCPM_Heatmap_w_logFC.pdf"))

# Open a new Cairo device with specified dimensions
library(Cairo)
CairoPDF(file = pdf_file, width=5, height=10, pointsize = 12, bg = "transparent", onefile = TRUE, canvas = "white")

# Combine the heatmap and additional legend
draw(heatmap, annotation_legend_list = list(logFC_legend), merge_legend = TRUE)

dev.off()
```

# MA Plot

```{r fig.width=5, fig.height=4}
library(edgeR)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

de_genes_annotated <- OvY_HSC_DEGs_FDR_p05_Granges
# Create a column for coloring points
de_genes_annotated$color <- "grey"
de_genes_annotated$color[de_genes_annotated$logFC > 1 & de_genes_annotated$FDR < 0.05] <- "red"
de_genes_annotated$color[de_genes_annotated$logFC < -1 & de_genes_annotated$FDR < 0.05] <- "blue"

# Create the MA plot
p <- ggplot(de_genes_annotated, aes(x = logCPM, y = logFC)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = color), alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_identity() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Average log CPM", y = "log2 Fold Change",
       title = "Differentially expressed genes\nOld vs Young, FDR < 0.05") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "darkgrey") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "black")+
  custom_theme

# Display the plot
print(p)

# To label specific genes, you can create a subset of genes to label
# For example, let's label the top 10 most significant genes
top_genes <- de_genes_annotated[order(de_genes_annotated$FDR),][1:10,]

# Add labels to the plot
p_labeled <- p +
  geom_text_repel(data = top_genes, 
                  aes(label = gene_name),
                  size = 4,
                  box.padding = unit(0.35, "lines"),
                  point.padding = unit(0.3, "lines"))

# Display the labeled plot
print(p_labeled)

# Define the directory
```

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=3}
filtered_genes <- granges_df[granges_df$seqnames %in% c(1:19, "X"), ]

filtered_genes$Direction <- ifelse(filtered_genes$logFC > 0, "Upregulated", "Downregulated")

# Count differentially expressed genes by chromosome and direction
de_chrom_counts <- table(filtered_genes$seqnames, filtered_genes$Direction)

# Convert to a data frame for ggplot2
de_chrom_counts_df <- as.data.frame(de_chrom_counts)
colnames(de_chrom_counts_df) <- c("Chromosome", "Direction", "Count")

# Ensure Chromosome is a factor and order levels
de_chrom_counts_df$Chromosome <- factor(de_chrom_counts_df$Chromosome, levels = c(1:19, "X"))

# Ensure Direction is a factor and order levels
de_chrom_counts_df$Direction <- factor(de_chrom_counts_df$Direction, levels = c("Upregulated", "Downregulated"))

# Plot using ggplot2 with custom theme
ggplot(de_chrom_counts_df, aes(x = Chromosome, y = Count, fill = Direction)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Upregulated" = "red", "Downregulated" = "blue")) +
  labs(title = "Differentially Expressed Genes by Chromosome",
       x = "Chromosome",
       y = "Count") +
  custom_theme +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "top")


```
